verdict.summary: The revision fixes the modeled off-retry/shared-vote ownership defect by latching unknown ICLK ownership and refusing normal retries, but enabled reboot and platform-shutdown cleanup still perform sensor/CSI stop and thread-deinit operations without consulting the latch. Safe shutdown/reboot, stream quiescence, and DMA safety are therefore unestablished.
verdict.scope: Independent host-only source and extracted-C review; no kernel, provider, device, camera, or physical-clock acceptance.

findings.title: Modeled shared-vote retry is quarantined after failed selected-gate restoration
findings.evidence: After off returns -EUCLEAN for incomplete restoration, the caller retains ON, latches UNKNOWN, and later on/off return before clock callbacks. The extracted fake-clock model verifies a subsequent off does not decrement the remaining unrelated selected-gate reference.
findings.limitation: This validates source sequencing and an aggregate-vote model; it does not execute Linux clock-provider accounting or physical hardware.

findings.title: Platform shutdown and registered reboot cleanup bypass unknown-ICLK quarantine
findings.evidence: is_cleanup calls is_sensor_front_stop for a probed front-started sensor without checking IS_SENSOR_ICLK_UNKNOWN. is_shutdown calls is_cleanup and then deinitializes sensor threads/cancels work without a latch check. The enabled and registered reboot handler also calls is_cleanup. is_sensor_front_stop/is_sensor_stop can issue module s_stream(false), CSI s_stream(IS_DISABLE_STREAM), and is_itf_stream_off calls.
findings.consequence: A quarantined sensor can still enter hardware-facing stop/deinit operations during shutdown or reboot. This source path prevents a safe-lifecycle claim; it does not by itself prove a physical adverse result.

findings.title: Terminal retention does not prove provider state, DMA quiescence, or generic parent lifetime
findings.evidence: is_disable's negative result is only a clock lookup failure before the void clk_disable_unprepare call. VFS ignores release's return, V4L2 unconditionally drops its node reference, and final video-device release frees the node; the patch takes one idempotent node and module pin per retained context and skips normal VB2/context frees. In the exact inspected source, core is freed only on probe error and no platform .remove callback is declared.
findings.consequence: The retained queue/buffers/context are an intentional terminal leak, not proof of stopped asynchronous work or safe DMA. The device ref is not a generic parent-allocation ref; exact current core lifetime source facts do not certify altered/external teardown.
